# Agent License

> Signed agent licenses that say which agent is calling, who it acts for, and what it may do. Checked at a checkpoint outside the agent.

Agent License is a prototype of agent identity and delegated authority. An issuer signs a license. The agent presents that license and a per-call justification. A checkpoint checks the signature, the mandate, the delegation chain, and a Cedar policy, then appends the decision to a Merkle log. The CLI is `agentlicense`. The SDK entry point is `licensed(fetch)` from `@agentlicense/sdk`.

This repository is a prototype. Services bind to localhost. The npm packages are not published yet.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/docs/quickstart/): Install Agent License, create keys, and issue a signed agent credential you can inspect and check.
- [Concepts](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/docs/concepts/): Agent identity, the three mandates, delegation, checkpoints, Cedar policy, and the Merkle decision log.
- [CLI reference](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/docs/cli/): Every agentlicense command and flag, generated from agentlicense --help.
- [SDK reference](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/docs/sdk/): Call a checkpoint with licensed(fetch), and use the core API to issue, verify, attenuate, and explain an agent credential.
- [Running a checkpoint](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/docs/checkpoint/): Start the local issuer, checkpoint, Cedar PDP, and Merkle log, then verify a decision.
- [FAQ](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/docs/faq/): Which agent is calling, how a license differs from a guess, and what this prototype does not do.

## Optional

- [License format](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town/blob/main/spec/LICENSE-FORMAT.md): Byte-level rules for the license, justification, and log
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): MCP gateway and the limits of this prototype
- [Repository](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town): Source, issues, and the `agentlicense` CLI
- [Proposed descriptor](https://mlescaille.github.io/agent-town/.well-known/agent-license.json): Not an IANA registration. The running PDP's AuthZEN discovery document is separate

# Documentation

Agent License is a prototype of agent identity and delegated authority. An issuer signs a license that names the agent, the user it acts for, and what it may do. A checkpoint outside the agent checks that credential on every call.

| Page | What it covers |
| --- | --- |

# Quickstart

These commands issue a license, show who it names, and dry-run one call. They run on your machine. Nothing listens on a public address.

You need Node.js 22 or newer and pnpm 9. The packages are not on the npm registry yet. Names reserved for publish are `agentlicense`, `@agentlicense/sdk`, and `@agentlicense/core`.

## Install from a clone

```sh
git clone \
  https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town.git
cd agent-town
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm exec agentlicense --help
```

`pnpm install` builds the packages. The repository is private until its owner makes it public, so the clone works for people who already have access. After a publish, the same CLI is `npm install -g agentlicense`.

`npm install github:mlescaille/agent-town` installs this repository as a package and builds it, once npm can read the repository. The command name is still `agentlicense`.

## Keys

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense keys init
```

That writes Ed25519 keys for an issuer, a log, `user:alice`, and two agents (`planner` and `researcher`) under `.agent-license/`. The directory is local and is not committed.

## Issue a user_goal license

The user key signs the request. The issuer key signs the license. The compact JWS is printed on stdout.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense issue \
  --user alice \
  --agent planner \
  --mandate user_goal \
  --goal "Summarize the primary calendar" \
  --actions calendar.read,calendar.create \
  --locations calendar:primary \
  --budget 10 \
  --ttl 3600 > license.jwt
```

## Inspect

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense inspect "$(cat license.jwt)"
```

`inspect` prints the agent id, the user, the mandate, the scope, and the delegation chain. With the key directory in place it also checks the issuer signature.

## Check a call

This asks the Cedar policy without starting the services and without writing the log.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense check \
  --license "$(cat license.jwt)" \
  --action calendar.read \
  --location calendar:primary \
  --why "Reading today's events is how the summary gets its facts."
```

A call outside the license is denied:

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense check \
  --license "$(cat license.jwt)" \
  --action mail.send \
  --location mail:outbox \
  --why "Sending mail is outside the calendar summary."
```

## Hand a narrower license to a sub-agent

Scope, budget, and expiry can shrink. They cannot grow, and the mandate type stays the same.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense attenuate \
  --parent "$(cat license.jwt)" \
  --agent researcher \
  --actions calendar.read \
  --locations calendar:primary \
  --budget 3 \
  --ttl 600 > child.jwt
```

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense inspect "$(cat child.jwt)"
```

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense check \
  --license "$(cat child.jwt)" \
  --action calendar.read \
  --location calendar:primary \
  --why "The sub-agent only reads the calendar it was given."
```

## The other two mandates

`direct_request` names one action and one location. The checkpoint allows only that pair.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense issue \
  --user alice \
  --agent planner \
  --mandate direct_request \
  --action calendar.read \
  --location calendar:primary \
  --budget 1 \
  --ttl 600 > direct.jwt
```

`agent_initiated` is the agent acting on its own, inside a fixed read-only ceiling.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense issue \
  --user alice \
  --agent planner \
  --mandate agent_initiated \
  --actions clock.read,catalog.list,memory.read \
  --locations clock:local,catalog:public,memory:self \
  --budget 5 \
  --ttl 600 > initiated.jwt
```

## Verify the log

`check` does not append decisions. `log verify` with no server replays the files under `.agent-license/log/`. Right after `keys init` that log is empty, and an empty log still verifies.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense log verify
```

To append decisions, start the stack with `agentlicense dev` and then verify the URL. That is covered in [Running a checkpoint](checkpoint.md).

---

# Concepts

An agent does not mint its own authority. A separate issuer signs a license. The agent presents that license, plus a signed reason for this call, to a checkpoint that is not the agent process. The checkpoint decides, records the decision, and only then forwards the call.

That is the answer to "which agent is calling my API": the caller presents an agent credential, the credential names a user it acts for, and a component outside the agent checks both.

## License

A license is a compact JWS (`typ` `agent-license+jwt`) signed by the issuer with Ed25519. It names:

- `sub`, the user, such as `user:alice`
- `agent`, a SPIFFE-style id such as `spiffe://agent-license.example/agent/planner`
- one mandate
- one `authorization_details` entry (`urn:agent-license:tool`) with actions, locations, and an optional call budget
- `txn` and `req_hash`, binding the license to the user-signed request
- `act`, the delegation chain

The issuer id and the checkpoint audience in this prototype are logical names, not hosts you can dial: `https://issuer.agent-license.example` and `https://checkpoint.agent-license.example`.

Agents never sign licenses. They sign a short-lived justification (`agent-justification+jwt`) for one action and one location.

## Mandates

A license carries exactly one mandate.

| Mandate | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `direct_request` | The user asked for this exact action and location. The scope is that one pair. |
| `user_goal` | The user set a goal. The agent chooses calls inside the granted scope. The justification restates that goal. |
| `agent_initiated` | The agent acts on its own, inside a fixed ceiling: `clock.read`, `catalog.list`, and `memory.read` on `clock:local`, `catalog:public`, and `memory:self`, with at most 5 calls. |

The justification basis has to match the mandate: `user_request`, `user_goal`, or `agent`. A read verb is `read`, `list`, or `get`. Every other verb is a write. `agent_initiated` cannot write.

## Delegation chain

`act` is the actor claim from RFC 8693. The outermost actor is the agent presenting the license. A nested `act` is the previous agent. The chain is at most eight agents, and no agent id repeats.

On current `main`, `agentlicense inspect` prints that chain as identifiers. A root license is the user, then the agent:

```text
chain
  user:alice
  spiffe://agent-license.example/agent/planner
```

An attenuated license adds the child at the end and sets `parent_jti`. Attenuation can narrow actions, locations, budget, and expiry. It cannot widen them, and it cannot change the mandate type.

### Canonical sentence

A single English sentence for the chain is not on `main`. It is only in open [pull request #1](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town/pull/1). That pull request would have `inspect` print a sentence of this shape:

> I am Researcher (subagent-123), acting on behalf of Planner (planner-1), on behalf of user:alice, requesting documents.search.

Until that pull request merges, the checkpoint does not require the sentence, and `attenuate` does not take `--name`, `--instance`, or `--task`. The on-behalf-of relationship that exists today is the nested `act` claim.

## Checkpoint

The checkpoint is a policy enforcement point outside the agent. `licensed(fetch)` posts the tool call to the checkpoint and sets two headers:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Agent-License` | The issuer-signed license |
| `Agent-Justification` | A new agent-signed justification for this call |

The JSON body carries `action`, `resource` (`type` and `id`), optional `input`, and an optional `user_request` JWS. The URL the agent passed to `fetch` is not contacted. The checkpoint owns the upstream.

`agentlicense dev` binds the checkpoint to `127.0.0.1:43122`. `POST /v1/invoke` is the only call path. `GET /health` reports that the process is up.

## Policy

The checkpoint sends an [OpenID AuthZEN 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/authorization-api-1_0.html) evaluation to a Cedar policy decision point. The policies in `policies/mandates.cedar` are:

- `permit-bound-call`, when the justification, scope, request binding, budget, chain, mandate, and basis all check out
- `forbid-agent-initiated-writes`
- `forbid-direct-request-inexact`, when a direct request is not exactly the named action and location

The decision point in this prototype trusts the booleans the checkpoint computed (`in_scope`, `basis_ok`, and the rest) and is meant to stay on localhost. Its discovery document is real: `GET /.well-known/authzen-configuration` on the PDP process.

## Log

Allowed and denied calls are appended to a Merkle log. The log signs each tree head (`agent-log-sth+jwt`). `agentlicense log verify` replays the entries and checks inclusion and consistency. A flipped leaf fails verification.

The log key can rewrite history if an observer did not keep an older signed tree head. [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) records that limit.

## What is not a registered discovery document

`GET /.well-known/authzen-configuration` on the running PDP is the AuthZEN discovery document this code serves.

`/.well-known/agent-license.json` on this website is a proposed descriptor for people and agents. It is not registered with IANA. The checkpoint does not fetch it. The fields in it match this prototype: header names, token `typ` values, mandate names, and `POST /v1/invoke`. Treat the file as documentation in JSON, not as a protocol the services implement.

---

# CLI reference

<!-- Contributors: edit the help text in packages/cli/src/main.ts, then run pnpm render-docs. Do not edit this file by hand. -->

Every command and flag of `agentlicense`, taken from `agentlicense --help`.

agentlicense — verifiable mandates for AI agents

Signed licenses for agent identity and delegated authority. An issuer signs a license that names the agent, who it acts for, and what it may do. A checkpoint outside the agent checks that license on every call.

## Usage

```sh
agentlicense --help
agentlicense keys init \
  [--home <dir>]
agentlicense issue \
  --user <name> \
  --agent <name> \
  --mandate <mandate> \
  [flags]
agentlicense inspect <license> \
  [--home <dir>]
agentlicense attenuate \
  --parent <license> \
  --agent <name> \
  [flags]
agentlicense check \
  --license <license> \
  --action <name> \
  --location <type:id> \
  [flags]
agentlicense log verify \
  [--url <url>] \
  [--home <dir>]
agentlicense dev [--home <dir>]
```

The default key directory is ./.agent-license. issue and attenuate print a compact JWS on stdout. Notes go to stderr.

## keys init

Write Ed25519 keys for the issuer, the log, user:alice, planner, and researcher.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license |

## issue

Sign a license. Requires --user, --agent, and --mandate. The named user's key signs the request. The issuer key signs the license. direct_request needs exactly one action and one location. user_goal needs --goal. agent_initiated must stay inside the read-only ceiling: clock.read, catalog.list, memory.read and clock:local, catalog:public, memory:self, with budget at most 5.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license |
| `--user <name>` | Required. User name, or user:<name>. |
| `--agent <name>` | Required. Agent slug, or a spiffe:// id. |
| `--mandate <mandate>` | Required. direct_request, user_goal, or agent_initiated. |
| `--goal <text>` | Required for user_goal. The goal the user set. |
| `--action <name>` | One action, such as calendar.read. |
| `--location <type:id>` | One location, such as calendar:primary. |
| `--actions <list>` | Comma-separated actions. |
| `--locations <list>` | Comma-separated locations. |
| `--budget <n>` | max_calls for this license. |
| `--ttl <seconds>` | Lifetime in seconds. Default: 3600. |

## inspect

Print the claims and the delegation chain. Checks the issuer signature when the key directory has an issuer key.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<license>` | Positional compact JWS. |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license |

## attenuate

Sign a narrower license for a sub-agent. Scope, budget, and expiry can shrink. They cannot grow, and the mandate type cannot change.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license |
| `--parent <license>` | Required. Parent compact JWS. |
| `--agent <name>` | Required. Child agent slug, or a spiffe:// id. |
| `--actions <list>` | Comma-separated actions. Default: the parent's actions. |
| `--locations <list>` | Comma-separated locations. Default: the parent's locations. |
| `--budget <n>` | max_calls. Cannot exceed the parent. |
| `--ttl <seconds>` | Lifetime. Must expire no later than the parent. |

## check

Dry-run one call against the Cedar policy. Does not start services and does not append to the log.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license |
| `--license <license>` | Required. Compact JWS. |
| `--action <name>` | Required. |
| `--location <type:id>` | Required. |
| `--why <text>` | Why this call is being made. Used when --justification is omitted. |
| `--justification <jws>` | Pre-signed justification. Default: sign one with the agent key. |
| `--user-request <jws>` | Originating user-request JWS. Checked when present. |
| `--basis <basis>` | user_request, user_goal, or agent. Default: the basis the mandate requires. |

## log verify

Replay the Merkle decision log and check inclusion and consistency.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license. Supplies the log public key, and the local log when --url is omitted. |
| `--url <url>` | Log base URL, for example http://127.0.0.1:43124. |

## dev

Start the issuer, checkpoint, Cedar PDP, Merkle log, and demo tool on 127.0.0.1. Ports: issuer 43121, checkpoint 43122, pdp 43123, log 43124, upstream 43125. Creates the key directory when it is missing. Runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Key directory. Default: .agent-license |

# SDK reference

`@agentlicense/sdk` exports one function, `licensed(fetch)`. `@agentlicense/core` is the library that issues and checks licenses. Both are ESM, for Node.js 22 or newer.

They are not on the npm registry yet. From a clone, `pnpm install` links them. After publish:

```text
npm install @agentlicense/sdk
```

That installs `@agentlicense/core` as well.

## licensed(fetch)

`licensed(baseFetch, options)` returns a function with the fetch signature. Each call posts JSON to `{checkpoint}/v1/invoke` and sets `Agent-License` and `Agent-Justification`. The request URL is ignored. The JSON body must include `action` and `resource` with `type` and `id`.

| Option | Required | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `license` | yes | Compact issuer-signed license |
| `agentPrivateKey` | yes | Private key of the agent named by the license |
| `checkpoint` | yes | Origin of the checkpoint, such as `http://127.0.0.1:43122` |
| `why` | yes | A string, or a function of `{ action, location }` |
| `userRequest` | no | User-request JWS. The checkpoint checks its hash when present |

The justification basis is chosen from the mandate. For `user_goal` the goal is copied from the license. The justification lives at most 300 seconds; the helper uses 60.

## Runnable example

`examples/sdk-quickstart/main.mjs` issues a `user_goal` license and presents it. Without `CHECKPOINT`, it uses a stand-in fetch and prints the headers. With `CHECKPOINT` set to a running `agentlicense dev`, it calls that checkpoint. Set `AGENT_LICENSE_HOME` to the same key directory `dev` is using, or the issuer signature will not match.

<!-- include:examples/sdk-quickstart/main.mjs -->

From the repository root, after `pnpm install`:

```sh
pnpm --filter @agent-license/sdk-quickstart start
```

Against a local checkpoint that was started with the default key directory:

```sh
AGENT_LICENSE_HOME=.agent-license \
  CHECKPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:43122 \
  pnpm --filter @agent-license/sdk-quickstart start
```

## Core API

Import from `@agentlicense/core`. The calls below are the ones the CLI and the checkpoint use.

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `initKeystore(home)` | Writes issuer, log, `user:alice`, `planner`, and `researcher` keys |
| `loadKeystore(home)` | Reads that directory |
| `generateEd25519Keypair()` | One Ed25519 key, `kid` set to the RFC 7638 thumbprint |
| `publicJwk(key)` | Public OKP JWK |
| `userIdOf(name)` / `agentSpiffe(name)` | `user:alice` and `spiffe://agent-license.example/agent/planner` |
| `createUserRequest(input)` | User-signed `agent-request+jwt` |
| `issueLicense(input)` | Issuer-signed license bound to that request |
| `verifyLicense(jws, issuerPublic)` | Signature, time window, and claim shape |
| `attenuateLicense(input)` | Narrower child license |
| `createJustification(input)` | Agent-signed justification |
| `verifyJustification(jws, agentPublic)` | Checks that justification |
| `assessPresentation(input)` | License, justification, scope, budget, chain, and basis |
| `delegationChain(claims)` | User, then agents from the original to the current |
| `expectedBasis(mandateType)` | `user_request`, `user_goal`, or `agent` |
| `parseLicenseClaims` / `decodeJws` | Parse without trusting a signature |
| `MerkleLog` | Append-only tree of decision records |
| `verifyReplayedLog(entries, sths, logPublic)` | Inclusion and consistency over a saved log |
| `LicenseError` | `error.code` is a stable string such as `malformed` or `expired` |

`issueLicense` returns `{ license, claims }`. `authorization_details` has exactly one element. Unknown claim names are rejected.

Constants worth knowing: `LICENSE_TYP`, `REQUEST_TYP`, `JUSTIFICATION_TYP`, `STH_TYP`, `AGENT_INITIATED_CEILING`, `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` (8), and `MAX_JUSTIFICATION_TTL_SECONDS` (300).

The demo at `examples/demo` runs the same API against the services: three mandates, an over-scope denial, attenuation, and a log replay. `pnpm demo` prints `demo: ok` when that walkthrough passes.

---

# Running a checkpoint

`agentlicense dev` starts five processes on `127.0.0.1`. They share the key directory. This is the prototype's whole deployment: one machine, no public listener.

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense dev
```

| Port | Process | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 43121 | Issuer | Signs licenses and attenuated licenses |
| 43122 | Checkpoint | Checks the caller, then forwards the tool call |
| 43123 | Cedar PDP | AuthZEN evaluation |
| 43124 | Log | Merkle decisions and proofs |
| 43125 | Demo tool | Upstream the checkpoint calls when the decision is allow |

If `.agent-license/` is missing, `dev` creates it. The process runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM.

Health checks, from another shell:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:43121/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:43122/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:43123/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:43123/.well-known/authzen-configuration
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:43124/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:43125/health
```

The AuthZEN document on port 43123 is served by the PDP. It points at `/access/v1/evaluation` on that same process.

## Present a license

With `dev` running, the SDK quickstart can use the same keys:

```sh
AGENT_LICENSE_HOME=.agent-license \
  CHECKPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:43122 \
  pnpm --filter @agent-license/sdk-quickstart start
```

The agent posts to `http://127.0.0.1:43122/v1/invoke` with `Agent-License` and `Agent-Justification`. An allow is HTTP 200 and includes the upstream result. A deny is HTTP 403 and still has a `log_index`, because the denial is recorded before the tool is contacted.

Issuer routes, if you sign without the CLI:

| Method and path | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/licenses` | `{ "user_request": "<jws>", "ttl_seconds": 3600 }` |
| `POST /v1/licenses/attenuate` | `{ "parent": "<jws>", "agent": "<spiffe id>", "authorization_details": [], "exp": 1700000000 }` |
| `GET /jwks` | Issuer, user, and agent public keys |

## Verify the log

After at least one invoke:

```sh
pnpm exec agentlicense log verify --url http://127.0.0.1:43124
```

That downloads the entries and signed tree heads, replays them, and checks an inclusion proof and a consistency proof. `ok true` means the replay matched. The log public key comes from `--home` (default `.agent-license`).

`log verify` without `--url` reads `.agent-license/log/entries.ndjson` and `sths.ndjson` instead of the network.

## What this process is not

The checkpoint does not authenticate itself to the policy decision point. Budgets live in the checkpoint process and reset when it exits. A checkpoint cannot re-prove that an ancestor scope was narrowed unless it is shown the parent license. Do not put these ports on a network.

---

# FAQ

## Which agent is calling my API?

The one named by the `Agent-License` header, if the checkpoint accepts the signature, the lifetime, the scope, the delegation chain, and the mandate. The license `agent` claim is a SPIFFE-style id. `sub` is the user that agent acts for. A justification signed by that agent's key says why this call is the one being made. The checkpoint is outside the agent, so the agent does not grade its own homework.

## Is this authentication or authorization?

Both, in a small way. The signatures are how the checkpoint authenticates the issuer and the agent. The mandate, the scope, and the Cedar policy are the authorization decision. A valid signature with the wrong action is still a deny.

## What is an on-behalf-of chain?

The license `act` claim, from RFC 8693. Each nested actor delegated to the next. The outermost actor is the agent making the call. On current `main`, `inspect` prints those ids. The English sentence ("I am Researcher, acting on behalf of Planner, on behalf of user:alice") is only in open [pull request #1](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town/pull/1).

## Can an agent widen its license?

No. Attenuation can drop actions, drop locations, lower `max_calls`, and shorten `exp`. It cannot add authority, and it cannot change `direct_request`, `user_goal`, or `agent_initiated` into a different mandate.

## Does this speak MCP?

Not yet. The checkpoint is an HTTP proxy in front of one demo tool. [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/mlescaille/agent-town/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) describes a later gateway where `tools/call` would require a license and `tools/list` would be filtered to the license scope. Nothing in this repository speaks the Model Context Protocol today.

## Is the npm package installable?

The names `agentlicense`, `@agentlicense/sdk`, and `@agentlicense/core` are the publish names. They are not on the registry until someone pushes a `v*` tag and the publish workflow runs with an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Until then, clone the repository and use pnpm. `npm install github:mlescaille/agent-town` is the git install, and it needs the repository to be readable by npm.

## Why does `agentlicense dev` bind to localhost?

The issuer, the policy decision point, and the log share a key directory and trust each other without authentication. That is acceptable for a prototype on `127.0.0.1` and unsafe anywhere else.

## What does the website's well-known file mean?

`/.well-known/agent-license.json` describes this project for agents that fetch the site. It is proposed, not an IANA registration, and the services do not fetch it. The PDP's `/.well-known/authzen-configuration` is different: that route exists in the running process and follows OpenID AuthZEN.

## What is deliberately unfinished?

Revocation before `exp`, budgets that survive a restart, a mandatory user-request presentation, ancestor scopes embedded so a checkpoint can re-check attenuation, and a second log so a replaced log key is visible to someone who kept an older tree head. Those are listed in the roadmap. This repository is not a production trust service.
